blocks.text: I can appreciate that a function is a mathematical relationship that uniquely maps a set of numbers onto another set of numbers.

items.title: Identifying functions
items.sub: what is, and is not, a function

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A function is a mathematical relationship that uniquely maps values of one set to the values of another set.
The domain of a function is the set of values that the mapping is performed on.
The range of a function is the set of values mapped to by the function and the stated domain.

slides.title: A function has inputs and outputs

blocks.text: A function takes an input and performs a series of operations, leading to an output. For any valid input, there is an output.
The function ×2 maps the inputs 0 to 5 onto the outputs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

blocks.label: What does “uniquely maps” mean?
blocks.text: The function ×2 uniquely maps 1 to 2 and to no other value. Each input goes to its own output.

slides.title: Domain and range on a graph

blocks.text: If x goes through the function ×2, the output is 2x. This is the graph of the function 2x (the graph of y = 2x).
When graphing functions we call the x values the {domain} and the y values the {range}.

items: The domain is on the horizontal axis.
The range is on the vertical axis.
Our domain is mapped onto our range.

rows.note: The graph of this function is called the graph of the function 3x − 1.

blocks.q: On the graph of a function, which axis shows the range?
blocks.why: The domain is the horizontal axis and the range is the vertical axis.

blocks.q: Which word describes the set of inputs to a function?
blocks.why: The set of inputs is called the domain.

blocks.text: Sofia graphs the function x². She says: “You can square negative numbers, so the range includes −3, −2 and −1.”

blocks.label: Is Sofia right?
blocks.text: Watch out! She had the labels the wrong way round. −3, −2 and −1 are in the **domain** of x² but not in the range. The function x² has no values below zero, so its range is greater than or equal to zero.
Now the function 1 − x². For example, 2 maps to 1 − 2² = −3 and 3 maps to 1 − 3² = −8.

blocks.label: What is the range of 1 − x²?
blocks.text: You will not find any output above 1, so the range is less than or equal to 1.

slides.title: In the domain only, or in both?

blocks.text: The function is x² + 2. You can square any number, so every number is a valid input (it is in the domain). Its outputs are never below 2.

blocks.q: Is each value in the domain only, or in both the domain and the range of x² + 2?
columns: In both the domain and the range

blocks.label: Check some
blocks.text: x = 0 gives 0² + 2 = 2, x = 2 gives 2² + 2 = 6 and x = 3 gives 3² + 2 = 11, so 2, 6 and 11 are outputs. Nothing below 2 can be an output.
To be a function, every value in the domain must be able to be mapped to a value in the range.
The function 1/x is not valid as it stands: x = 0 is not a valid input, because dividing by 0 is undefined.
We make it a valid function by {restricting the domain}: “x can be any value except 0”. A restriction on the domain defines the invalid inputs.
Some functions are already valid for every x. For example, 3 − 2x has no x value we cannot input.

blocks.q: Which restriction makes each function valid?

options: x can be any value except −3
x can be any value except 3
x can be any value except 6
x can be any value except −6
x can be any value except 0
x can be any value except 5
x can be any value except 0
x can be any value except 3
x can be any value except 7

blocks.text: For the function 2x, one input uniquely maps to one output. That makes 2x a {one-to-one} function.
For the function x², many inputs uniquely map to the same one output. For example, −1 and 1 both map to 1, and −2 and 2 both map to 4. That makes x² a {many-to-one} function.
Both one-to-one and many-to-one relationships make valid functions.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Many functions with x² are many-to-one, but not all. The function 3x², where x is greater than or equal to 0, is one-to-one, because the domain restriction removes the negative inputs.
The function √x is one-to-one when x is greater than or equal to 0.
Positive or negative √x is different. The input 4 maps to both +2 and −2: one input maps to many, non-unique outputs. This is a one-to-many relationship.
One-to-many relationships are {not valid functions}. A function uniquely maps values of the domain to values of the range, and here 4 does not map uniquely to +2 or to −2.

blocks.q: Does each relationship make a valid function?

items.q: The input 3 maps to 9, and the input −3 also maps to 9.
The input 25 maps to both 5 and −5.

slides.title: Checking and securing understanding of functions

items: A function is a mathematical relationship that uniquely maps values of one set to the values of another set.
The set of inputs is the domain and the set of outputs is the range.
Functions that uniquely map each value in their domain to one value in their range are one-to-one.
If many values in the domain map to the same value in the range, the function is many-to-one.
One-to-many functions do not exist, because they do not uniquely map each value in their domain.

flashcards.back: A mathematical relationship that uniquely maps values of one set to the values of another set.

flashcards.front: What is the domain of a function?
flashcards.back: The set of values that the mapping is performed on (the inputs).

flashcards.front: What is the range of a function?
flashcards.back: The set of values mapped to by the function and the stated domain (the outputs).

flashcards.front: On a graph, which axis is the domain and which is the range?
flashcards.back: The horizontal axis is the domain (the x values). The vertical axis is the range (the y values).

flashcards.front: What is the range of the function x²?
flashcards.back:
Greater than or equal to zero.

The function x² has no values below zero.

flashcards.front: What is the range of the function 1 − x²?
Why is x = 0 not a valid input for 1/x?
flashcards.back:
Dividing by 0 is undefined.

We restrict the domain: “x can be any value except 0”.

flashcards.front: What does it mean to restrict the domain?
flashcards.back: It is a restriction on the domain that defines the invalid inputs, so the relationship becomes a valid function.

One input uniquely maps to one output.

Example: 2x.

Many inputs uniquely map to the same one output.

Example: x² maps both −2 and 2 to 4.

flashcards.front: Is a one-to-many relationship a valid function?
flashcards.back:
No. One input maps to many, non-unique outputs.

Example: positive or negative √x maps 4 to both +2 and −2.

flashcards.front: Is 3x², where x is greater than or equal to 0, one-to-one or many-to-one?
flashcards.back: One-to-one. The domain restriction removes the negative inputs.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Checking and securing understanding of functions
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a number or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: For the function 5x − 4, what is the output when the input is 6?
The function halves x and then adds 4. What is the output when the input is 10?
For the function x² − 4x, what is the output when the input is 6?
The range of the function x² is “greater than or equal to” which number?
questions.explanation: The function x² has no values below zero.

questions.prompt: The range of the function 1 − x² is “less than or equal to” which number?
questions.explanation: 1 − x² can never be more than 1, because x² is never below 0.

questions.prompt: Which x value must be excluded from the domain of the function 6/(x + 3)?
questions.explanation: When x = −3 the denominator is 0, and dividing by 0 is undefined.

questions.prompt: For the function x², how many different inputs map to the output 9?
questions.explanation: Both 3 and −3 map to 9, so x² is many-to-one.

questions.prompt: Is 3x², where x is greater than or equal to 0, a one-to-one or a many-to-one function? Answer with one-to-one or many-to-one.
questions.explanation: The restriction removes the negative inputs, so each output comes from only one input.

questions.prompt: For the function x² − 4x, is the value −5 in the domain only, or in both the domain and the range? Answer domain only or both.
questions.explanation: x² − 4x is never below −4, so −5 is a valid input but never an output.

questions.prompt: Is “positive or negative √x” a valid function? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The input 4 maps to both 2 and −2, so it is one-to-many and does not uniquely map.
